Since the heading button text use a plain text field, I assume the current method isn’t an option. Potential solutions I can think of are:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Build the option to assign the lang as a field within the CTA that applies to the entire CTA block of code. This would solve the immediate issue, but feels like we’d be opening a can of worms since there’s other blocks on the site this may need to be built into.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. A more streamlined approach I think I favor is to force the declaration of the language that applies to the entire page (or at least anything rendered inside the <main> element, so that we can exclude the header and footer). My proposal for this method would be to build a language option for any content page on the site (ignoring other templated pages for now) so that the code would output something like <main class="relative" id=“mainContent” lang=“es”>. This would mean we’d need to split the current scholarships page into two versions: English and Spanish, but it would sidestep the issue of needing to specify langagues on such a granular level across many points in the system.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > What are your thoughts on this? I’m looking for the best solution that satisfies the WCAG 2.2 AA spec, doesn’t muddy the editing process, while also not creating a ton of work.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Build the option to assign the lang as a field within the CTA that applies to the entire CTA block of code. > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. A more streamlined approach I think I favor is to force the declaration of the language that applies to the entire page (or at least anything rendered inside the <main> element, so that we can exclude the header and footer). My proposal for this method would be to build a language option for any content page on the site (ignoring other templated pages for now) so that the code would output something like <main class="relative" id=“mainContent” lang=“es”>. This would mean we’d need to split the current scholarships page into two versions: English and Spanish, but it would sidestep the issue of needing to specify langagues on such a granular level across many points in the system.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Build the option to assign the lang as a field within the CTA that applies to the entire CTA block of code. > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. A more streamlined approach I think I favor is to force the declaration of the language that applies to the entire page (or at least anything rendered inside the <main> element, so that we can exclude the header and footer). My proposal for this method would be to build a language option for any content page on the site (ignoring other templated pages for now) so that the code would output something like <main class="relative" id=“mainContent” lang=“es”>. This would mean we’d need to split the current scholarships page into two versions: English and Spanish, but it would sidestep the issue of needing to specify langagues on such a granular level across many points in the system.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Build the option to assign the lang as a field within the CTA that applies to the entire CTA block of code. > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. A more streamlined approach I think I favor is to force the declaration of the language that applies to the entire page (or at least anything rendered inside the <main> element, so that we can exclude the header and footer). My proposal for this method would be to build a language option for any content page on the site (ignoring other templated pages for now) so that the code would output something like <main class="relative" id=“mainContent” lang=“es”>. This would mean we’d need to split the current scholarships page into two versions: English and Spanish, but it would sidestep the issue of needing to specify langagues on such a granular level across many points in the system.

In regard to the image usage, I’m pretty sure it’s not a CMS issue, but something programmatic. If this existed in the code before your work on the site, then we can shelve this. If there’s any chance it was caused by either the accessibility work or the Vue/Tailwind updates, I’d like to see if we can correct it. I’ll try to summarize as concisely as possible...

On the Red Brick Rec Center page, under “Features and Attractions” several of the photos being used don’t match the “Page Image” for the page they represent. Instead, the photo being used seems to pull from a “Photos” section that’s also part of those pages.

As a specific example, let’s use the Climbing Wall at the Red Brick. The “Page Image” for that entry is a wide-angle photo of the entire wall. On the Red Brick Rec Center page, the photo that’s showing isn’t the page image, it’s the one of a single foot on the climbing wall entered on the Climbing Wall page under “photos."

I’m guessing there’s something in the code that’s intended as a fallback that’s instead taking precedence where it shouldn’t. (i.e. if:photos are present, look for images in the entries’ photo collection and display the first one; else: display the page image. In practice, that should be reversed: display the page photo and fallback to the 1st photo if there’s no page image).

Hopefully all that makes sense.

This would mean we’d need to split the current scholarships page into two versions: English and Spanish, but it would sidestep the issue of needing to specify langagues on such a granular level across many points in the system.

Hi Shaun,

Hope your Monday was good.

As far as moving that field goes, yes very easy. That's a change you can
make in any environment that has allowAdminChanges on which allows access
to the settings option in the CMS. In this case, Settings > Fields > Matrix
> Sidebar Builder then scroll down to CTA under Block Types, then CTA under
fields. Finally, under configuration there's a list of fields with a handle
on the right which allows drag to reorder.

I've already implemented it for you, but just so you know for later. I can
provide a video of the process or do a screen share via Zoom if needed,
just let me know.

For the changes with language, it depends on what kind of change you need
to make. In the CKEditor, if you just need to remove the language from the
bar or turn on/off headings everywhere that description is used then yes,
that's easy.
[image: Screenshot 2025-10-13 at 2.03.53 PM.png]
If you need to add a language to the list, that's simple to do here and I
can provide a simple change for that if we need that later on. It's
possible there could be config changes required here later on--there's a
lot of options.
[image: Screenshot 2025-10-13 at 2.13.12 PM.png]

I think the most likely future adjustments are going to be turning the
"Description (with language)" on or off for specific areas. This is very
easy once you find the associated section in the CMS--I think you know as
well as I that's usually the hardest part.
 [image: Screenshot 2025-10-13 at 2.19.42 PM.png]

For the alt text, I'm going through the last folder (entry-types) now. As
soon as that's done I just need to text the fields and ensure they're
working as expected.

I've been called for Jury Duty today and I'm not sure how long that's going
to take so I will keep you apprised of what's going on.

Hi Eric,

AR-50/54: Also tested well and looks good to go.

AR-68: I think we might have (unfortunately) opened up a can of worms on this one. If you look at the scholarships page, there are also two sidebar items that are in Spanish. These items use the CTA block in craft and are designed to contain an image, heading, text content, and button. Since the heading button text use a plain text field, I assume the current method isn’t an option. Potential solutions I can think of are:

1. Build the option to assign the lang as a field within the CTA that applies to the entire CTA block of code. This would solve the immediate issue, but feels like we’d be opening a can of worms since there’s other blocks on the site this may need to be built into.
2. A more streamlined approach I think I favor is to force the declaration of the language that applies to the entire page (or at least anything rendered inside the <main> element, so that we can exclude the header and footer). My proposal for this method would be to build a language option for any content page on the site (ignoring other templated pages for now) so that the code would output something like <main class="relative" id=“mainContent” lang=“es”>. This would mean we’d need to split the current scholarships page into two versions: English and Spanish, but it would sidestep the issue of needing to specify langagues on such a granular level across many points in the system.

What are your thoughts on this? I’m looking for the best solution that satisfies the WCAG 2.2 AA spec, doesn’t muddy the editing process, while also not creating a ton of work.

Thanks,

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following system:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Okay, that clarification made quick work of three items--so I really appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up on since the fixes are all Craft > Settings solutions. Here are the 3 items and solutions:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Originally Item #2: Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example: https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times (see attached).
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. Originally Item #3: Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. Originally Item #5: The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)

   into.
   - *AR-25*: News container SR announcement - fixed previously, should be
   working
   - *AR-50*, *AR-54*: Both calendar issues - did need some updating
   between the *CalendarView* (added SR functions) and *CalendarViewHeader*
   (added detailed aria-labels + added support for enter/space press to
   activate), should be working now
   - *AR-68*: Language indicator on Scholarship / Financial Aid page - this
   one is a little tricky because the content is coming from the CMS, but it
   basically has two parts: rich text fields and custom builders. Fortunately
   CKEditor has native support for this so all we had to do was drag the
   language field into each rich text config and now it shows as an option--I
   did have to add spanish as an option via the JSON config code though. One
   minor gotcha with this is that when rich text fields are used only one
   language can be used at a time so the rich text for the Scholarships page
   will need to be split into two separate content articles to be
   accessibility compliant. The second part is the builder and I need to
   update the builder--sidebar.twig file for this which may include a new
   field option to indicate it's in Spanish - this solution is not yet in dev.

  So all that's pending for tomorrow is the language indicator and alt text
- I'll complete / tackle those tomorrow.

Then I'll jump back to Climb13ers.

>>>>>>>> click-away behavior on touch devices: when a top-level menu was open,

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Wed, Sep 24, 2025 at 9:58 PM Shaun Cooney |
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Monument Graphics <shaun@monumentgraphics.com> wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks as always for the update.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> use the following system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the alt text.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images,
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not,
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. *Originally Item #2*: Remove the “Daily"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    (see attached).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       “daily” value
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. *Originally Item #3*: Require cancellations
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    one of the fields therein to be required?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. *Originally Item #5*: The list of selectable
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> These will all need to be addressed as last minute
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> items since the "allowAdminChanges" must be on, which means we'll need to
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> use a production database in staging, then pushed to production with the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> other updates.

Either one means they can be marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following system:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Okay, that clarification made quick work of three items--so I really appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up on since the fixes are all Craft > Settings solutions. Here are the 3 items and solutions:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Originally Item #2: Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example: https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times (see attached).

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. Originally Item #3: Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Hi Eric,
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> If there’s a way encourage filling of the alt text,
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> that’s definitely good news! Hopefully the auto-popup works. When I last
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> discussed this with Aspen, the understanding was that the staff would need
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> to be trained on how to enter the alt text as part of their process, and
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the impetus would be on them to make sure it gets done. If there’s a way
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> when uploading images as part of other entries to force the alt text,
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> that’s even better.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Regarding the alt text settings per directory, I think
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> we just need to enable alt text across the board in all media directories.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> It should be *required* for the following:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Galleries
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Teasers
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Sliders
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Hero Images
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Articles (possibly?)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I’m still thoroughly confused as to why Mark set up
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> many directories. Some aren’t actively in use from what I see (Documents,
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Cover photos, Open Graph Images). Others seem to be used inconsistently
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> (i.e. the PDFs folder often ends up with images in there). The directories
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> don’t seem well organized, and stuff has a habit of going into the wrong
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> directory anyway, hence why I think alt text should at least be an option
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> for ALL media, but only required in the folders in which image content is
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the primary content allowed. If that proves to be an issue, please let me
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> know.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Is there a centralized location in Craft where we can
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> view what entries store conent in which media folders, or is that addressed
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> on a field by field basis? If there’s a central location, I’d like to take
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> a look at that.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> For point #3 in my last email regarding using
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> alt=“null” vs populating the alt text with a file name, I re-read the WCAG
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> spec and I think we’d be better off making the fallback alt=“”. While this
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> may trip up automted scanners, more often than not, I think one could make
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the argument that most images on the site do NOT convey essential
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> information and serve a mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> one means they can be marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> AA.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> If you run into any questions or have any concerns
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> about that approach, please let me know.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On Wed, Sep 24, 2025 at 9:58 PM Shaun Cooney | Monument
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Graphics <shaun@monumentgraphics.com> wrote:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks as always for the update.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the following system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the alt text.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. *Originally Item #2*: Remove the “Daily"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    (see attached).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       “daily” value
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. *Originally Item #3*: Require cancellations
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    one of the fields therein to be required?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. *Originally Item #5*: The list of selectable
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following system:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Okay, that clarification made quick work of three items--so I really appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up on since the fixes are all Craft > Settings solutions. > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Originally Item #2: Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example: https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times (see attached).
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. Originally Item #3: Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. Originally Item #5: The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks as always for the update.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the following system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the alt text.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Okay, that clarification made quick work of three

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> and solutions:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. *Originally Item #2*: Remove the “Daily"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    (see attached).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       “daily” value
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. *Originally Item #3*: Require cancellations
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    one of the fields therein to be required?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. *Originally Item #5*: The list of selectable
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> These will all need to be addressed as last minute
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> items since the "allowAdminChanges" must be on, which means we'll need to
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> use a production database in staging, then pushed to production with the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> other updates.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I wanted to let you know about them early in case you
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> want to try the solutions while you're looking over the site.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks as always for the update.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the following system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    alt text.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. *Originally Item #2*: Remove the “Daily"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    (see attached).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       “daily” value
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. *Originally Item #3*: Require cancellations
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    one of the fields therein to be required?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. *Originally Item #5*: The list of selectable
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> items since the "allowAdminChanges" must be on, which means we'll need to

<blockquote type="cite" style="border-left-color:grey;border-left-width:thin;border-left-style:solid;margin:5px;padding-left:10px">
<div dir="ltr">
<p style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">Hi Shaun,</p>
<p style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">Quick update on the mobile nav issue. The problem came from the click-away behavior on touch devices: when a top-level menu was open, scrolling inside a long submenu (e.g., Sports Activities → Youth Activities) could be interpreted as a tap on a link. That triggered navigation mid-scroll, which looked like the list didn’t finish loading.</p>
<p style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">I’ve added a guard so touch events inside the submenu don’t trigger link clicks while scrolling. Tapping links still works as expected; tapping outside still closes the menu.</p>
<p style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">Sandbox is ready to be tested again now. Let me know when you're ready to bring this one to production.</p>
<p style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">I also fixed the Today's Activities ordering issue this morning.</p>

<br>
Galleries<br>
Teasers<br>
Sliders<br>
Hero Images<br>
Articles (possibly?)<br>

I’m still thoroughly confused as to why Mark set up many directories. Some aren’t actively in use from what I see (Documents, Cover photos, Open Graph Images). The directories don’t seem well organized, and stuff has a habit of going into the wrong directory anyway, hence why I think alt text should at least be an option for ALL media, but only required in the folders in which image content is the primary content allowed. <br>
Is there a centralized location in Craft where we can view what entries store conent in which media folders, or is that addressed on a field by field basis? If there’s a central location, I’d like to take a look at that.<br>
<br>
For point #3 in my last email regarding using alt=“null” vs populating the alt text with a file name, I re-read the WCAG spec and I think we’d be better off making the fallback alt=“”. While this may trip up automted scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument that most images on the site do NOT convey essential information and serve a mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either one means they can be marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.<br>
<br>
If you run into any questions or have any concerns about that approach, please let me know.<br></div>

<div dir="ltr" class="gmail_attr">On Wed, Sep 24, 2025 at 9:58 PM Shaun Cooney | Monument Graphics &lt;<a href="mailto:shaun@monumentgraphics.com" target="_blank">shaun@monumentgraphics.com</a>&gt; wrote:<br></div>
<blockquote class="gmail_quote" style="margin:0px 0px 0px 0.8ex;border-left-width:1px;border-left-style:solid;padding-left:1ex;border-left-color:rgb(204,204,204)">
<div>
<div name="messageBodySection">
<div dir="auto">Thanks as always for the update.<br>
<br>
The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.&nbsp;<br>
<br>
In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following system:</div>
<ol type="1">
<li>If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.</li>
<li>If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)</li>
<li>For other images, such as hero images, featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.</li>
</ol>
<div dir="auto">Let me know what you think….<br>
<br>
In the meantime, I’ll start reviewing dev for the other items.<br></div>

<div name="messageReplySection">On Sep 24, 2025 at 10:26 AM -0600, Eric Phifer &lt;<a href="mailto:eric@ericphiferllc.com" target="_blank">eric@ericphiferllc.com</a>&gt;, wrote:<br>
<blockquote type="cite" style="border-left-width:thin;border-left-style:solid;margin:5px;padding-left:10px;border-left-color:grey">
<div dir="ltr">Okay, that clarification made quick work of three items--so I really appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up on since the fixes are all Craft &gt; Settings solutions. Here are the 3 items and solutions:
<div>
<ol>
<li><b>Originally Item #2</b>: Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example: <a href="https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times" target="_blank">https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times</a> (see attached).</li>
<ul>
<li><b>Solution</b>: Update in Settings &gt; Fields &gt; Dropdown &gt; Repeat Frequency &gt; check default Weekly (safest and quickest option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value</li>
</ul>
<li><b>Originally Item #3</b>: Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?</li>
<ul>
<li><b>Solution</b>: Update in Settings &gt; Fields &gt; Events &gt; Cancellations &gt; check “This field is required.”</li>
</ul>
<li><b>Originally Item #5</b>: The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?</li>
<ul>
<li><b>Solution</b>: Update in Settings &gt; Fields &gt; Entries &gt; Location Select &gt; Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)<br></li>
</ul>
</ol>
<div>These will all need to be addressed as last minute items since the "allowAdminChanges" must be on, which means we'll need to use a production database in staging, then pushed to production with the other updates.</div>
</div>
<div><br></div>
<div>I wanted to let you know about them early in case you want to try the solutions while you're looking over the site.</div>
<div><br></div>
<div>14 down, 12 items remaining now.</div>
</div>

<div name="messageReplySection">On Sep 3, 2025 at 5:32 PM -0600, Eric Phifer &lt;<a href="mailto:eric@ericphiferllc.com" target="_blank">eric@ericphiferllc.com</a>&gt;, wrote:<br>
<blockquote type="cite" style="border-left-width:thin;border-left-style:solid;margin:5px;padding-left:10px;border-left-color:grey">
<div dir="ltr">On the other issues:
<div>
<ul>
<li>The news filters have been notoriously finicky&nbsp;from page to page. I've sorted it out now--the "showNews" logic just needed to be tweaked a bit.</li>
<li>In terms of the slow load times, I've been seeing the same thing and this is last on my list to test and optimize after everything else is in place. Part of this will be fixing the placeholders which aren't resolving currently and you're right that production should improve it some.&nbsp;</li>
<li>Forestry page, the spacing and fonts have changed how they work from 1.9:</li>
<ul>
<li><em style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">v1.9 uses fixed design tokens defined in<span>&nbsp;</span><code style="font-family:monospace">tailwind.config.js</code><span>&nbsp;</span>(discrete spacing scale; static text sizes). v4 switches to CSS variables and formulas — spacing becomes “any integer ×<span>&nbsp;</span><code style="font-family:monospace">--spacing</code>,” and text sizes/line-heights come from<span>&nbsp;</span><code style="font-family:monospace">--text-*</code>variables — while<span>&nbsp;</span><code style="font-family:monospace">prose</code><span>&nbsp;</span>works the same but plugs into the new variable system.</em><span style="font-size:medium;color:rgb(0,0,0)"></span><br></li>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)"><span>For instance, the old system</span></font></li>
<ul>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)"><span>&lt;div class="mt-8 p-4"&gt;<br>
&nbsp; &lt;!-- mt-8 = 2rem (32px), p-4 = 1rem (16px) --&gt;<br></span></font></li>
</ul>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">The new system:</font></li>
<ul>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">&lt;div class="mt-8 p-4"&gt;<br>
&nbsp; &lt;!-- mt-8 = calc(var(--spacing) * 8)<br>
&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;p-4 = calc(var(--spacing) * 4)&nbsp;--&gt;<br></font></li>
</ul>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)"><span>I've been working on the base styling and I think I have things restored--there may still&nbsp;be some outliers. I removed the spacing definitions in app.pcss&nbsp;@theme section, which was a carryover from the tailwind.config.js v1.9 but seems to be interfering&nbsp;with the styling we want now.</span></font></li>
</ul>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)"><span>The accessibility checker issues:</span></font></li>
<ul>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)"><b>Four landmark issues</b>:&nbsp;</font></li>
<ul>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">navigation--top.vue has the &lt;div class="flex-grow"&gt;&nbsp;</font></li>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">navigation-item--secondary.twig has the &lt;span&gt; Activity Calendar &lt;/span&gt;</font></li>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)">To fix this accessibility issue I added a &lt;nav&gt; as a parent element to main navigation, main navigation items and "utility navigation items" for the secondary nav items which are all labelled now with aria-label</font></li>
</ul>
<li><font style="color:rgb(0,0,0)"></font></li>
</ul>

>>>> wrote:
>>>>
>>>> Hi Shaun,
>>>>
>>>> Quick update on the mobile nav issue. The problem came from the
>>>> click-away behavior on touch devices: when a top-level menu was open,
>>>> scrolling inside a long submenu (e.g., Sports Activities → Youth
>>>> Activities) could be interpreted as a tap on a link. That triggered
>>>> navigation mid-scroll, which looked like the list didn’t finish loading.
>>>>
>>>> I’ve added a guard so touch events inside the submenu don’t trigger
>>>> link clicks while scrolling. Tapping links still works as expected; tapping
>>>> outside still closes the menu.
>>>>
>>>> Sandbox is ready to be tested again now. Let me know when you're ready
>>>> to bring this one to production.
>>>>
>>>> I also fixed the Today's Activities ordering issue this morning.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks as always for the update.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> the following system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    alt text.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Okay, that clarification made quick work of three
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> items--so I really appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> on since the fixes are all Craft > Settings solutions. Here are the 3 items
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> and solutions:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. *Originally Item #2*: Remove the “Daily"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    (see attached).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       “daily” value
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. *Originally Item #3*: Require cancellations
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    one of the fields therein to be required?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. *Originally Item #5*: The list of selectable
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> These will all need to be addressed as last minute
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> items since the "allowAdminChanges" must be on, which means we'll need to
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> use a production database in staging, then pushed to production with the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> other updates.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I wanted to let you know about them early in case you
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> want to try the solutions while you're looking over the site.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    placeholders which aren't resolving currently and you're right that
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    production should improve it some.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - Forestry page, the spacing and fonts have
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    changed how they work from 1.9:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *v1.9 uses fixed design tokens defined
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       in tailwind.config.js (discrete spacing scale; static text sizes). v4
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       switches to CSS variables and formulas — spacing becomes “any integer
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       × --spacing,” and text sizes/line-heights come from --text-*variables —
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       while prose works the same but plugs into the new variable system.*
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - For instance, the old system
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = 2rem (32px), p-4 = 1rem
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          (16px) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - The new system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = calc(var(--spacing) * 8)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>                 p-4 = calc(var(--spacing) * 4) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - I've been working on the base styling
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       and I think I have things restored--there may still be some outliers. I
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       removed the spacing definitions in app.pcss @theme section, which was a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       carryover from the tailwind.config.js v1.9 but seems to be interfering with
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       the styling we want now.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - The accessibility checker issues:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Four landmark issues*:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation--top.vue has the <div
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          class="flex-grow">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation-item--secondary.twig has the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          <span> Activity Calendar </span>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - To fix this accessibility issue I added
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          a <nav> as a parent element to main navigation, main navigation items and
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          "utility navigation items" for the secondary nav items which are all
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          labelled now with aria-label

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Hi Eric,
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> If there’s a way encourage filling of the alt text, that’s
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> definitely good news! Hopefully the auto-popup works. When I last discussed
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> this with Aspen, the understanding was that the staff would need to be
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> trained on how to enter the alt text as part of their process, and the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> impetus would be on them to make sure it gets done. If there’s a way when
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> uploading images as part of other entries to force the alt text, that’s
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> even better.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Regarding the alt text settings per directory, I think we
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> just need to enable alt text across the board in all media directories. It
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> should be *required* for the following:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Galleries
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Teasers
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Sliders
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Hero Images
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Articles (possibly?)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I’m still thoroughly confused as to why Mark set up many
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> directories. Some aren’t actively in use from what I see (Documents, Cover
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> photos, Open Graph Images). Others seem to be used inconsistently (i.e. the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> PDFs folder often ends up with images in there). The directories don’t seem
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> well organized, and stuff has a habit of going into the wrong directory
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> anyway, hence why I think alt text should at least be an option for ALL
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> media, but only required in the folders in which image content is the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> primary content allowed. If that proves to be an issue, please let me know.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Is there a centralized location in Craft where we can view
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> what entries store conent in which media folders, or is that addressed on a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> field by field basis? If there’s a central location, I’d like to take a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> look at that.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> For point #3 in my last email regarding using alt=“null” vs
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> populating the alt text with a file name, I re-read the WCAG spec and I
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> think we’d be better off making the fallback alt=“”. While this may trip up
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> automted scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> that most images on the site do NOT convey essential information and serve
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> a mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either one means they can be
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> If you run into any questions or have any concerns about
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> that approach, please let me know.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Thanks as always for the update.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> following system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    alt text.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers,
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> Okay, that clarification made quick work of three
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> items--so I really appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> on since the fixes are all Craft > Settings solutions. Here are the 3 items
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> and solutions:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    1. *Originally Item #2*: Remove the “Daily"
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    (see attached).
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       “daily” value
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    2. *Originally Item #3*: Require cancellations
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    one of the fields therein to be required?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    3. *Originally Item #5*: The list of selectable
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields >
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> These will all need to be addressed as last minute items
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> since the "allowAdminChanges" must be on, which means we'll need to use a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> production database in staging, then pushed to production with the other
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> updates.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> I wanted to let you know about them early in case you
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> want to try the solutions while you're looking over the site.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On the other issues:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - The news filters have been notoriously
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    finicky from page to page. I've sorted it out now--the "showNews" logic
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    just needed to be tweaked a bit.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - In terms of the slow load times, I've been
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    seeing the same thing and this is last on my list to test and optimize
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    after everything else is in place. Part of this will be fixing the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    placeholders which aren't resolving currently and you're right that
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    production should improve it some.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - Forestry page, the spacing and fonts have
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    changed how they work from 1.9:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *v1.9 uses fixed design tokens defined
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       in tailwind.config.js (discrete spacing scale; static text sizes). v4
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       switches to CSS variables and formulas — spacing becomes “any integer
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       × --spacing,” and text sizes/line-heights come from --text-*variables —
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       while prose works the same but plugs into the new variable system.*
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - For instance, the old system
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = 2rem (32px), p-4 = 1rem
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          (16px) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - The new system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = calc(var(--spacing) * 8)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>                 p-4 = calc(var(--spacing) * 4) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - I've been working on the base styling
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       and I think I have things restored--there may still be some outliers. I
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       removed the spacing definitions in app.pcss @theme section, which was a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       carryover from the tailwind.config.js v1.9 but seems to be interfering with
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       the styling we want now.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - The accessibility checker issues:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Four landmark issues*:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation--top.vue has the <div
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          class="flex-grow">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation-item--secondary.twig has the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          <span> Activity Calendar </span>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - To fix this accessibility issue I added
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          a <nav> as a parent element to main navigation, main navigation items and
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          "utility navigation items" for the secondary nav items which are all
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          labelled now with aria-label
