>>>>>>>> If there’s a way encourage filling of the alt text, that’s
>>>>>>>> definitely good news! Hopefully the auto-popup works. When I last discussed
>>>>>>>> this with Aspen, the understanding was that the staff would need to be

>>>>>>>> impetus would be on them to make sure it gets done. If there’s a way when
>>>>>>>> uploading images as part of other entries to force the alt text, that’s
>>>>>>>> even better.
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> Regarding the alt text settings per directory, I think we just need
>>>>>>>> to enable alt text across the board in all media directories. It should be
>>>>>>>> *required* for the following:
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> Galleries
>>>>>>>> Teasers
>>>>>>>> Sliders
>>>>>>>> Hero Images
>>>>>>>> Articles (possibly?)
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> I’m still thoroughly confused as to why Mark set up many
>>>>>>>> directories. Some aren’t actively in use from what I see (Documents, Cover
>>>>>>>> photos, Open Graph Images). Others seem to be used inconsistently (i.e. the
>>>>>>>> PDFs folder often ends up with images in there). The directories don’t seem
>>>>>>>> well organized, and stuff has a habit of going into the wrong directory
>>>>>>>> anyway, hence why I think alt text should at least be an option for ALL
>>>>>>>> media, but only required in the folders in which image content is the
>>>>>>>> primary content allowed. If that proves to be an issue, please let me know.
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> Is there a centralized location in Craft where we can view what
>>>>>>>> entries store conent in which media folders, or is that addressed on a
>>>>>>>> field by field basis? If there’s a central location, I’d like to take a
>>>>>>>> look at that.
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> For point #3 in my last email regarding using alt=“null” vs
>>>>>>>> populating the alt text with a file name, I re-read the WCAG spec and I
>>>>>>>> think we’d be better off making the fallback alt=“”. While this may trip up
>>>>>>>> automted scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument
>>>>>>>> that most images on the site do NOT convey essential information and serve
>>>>>>>> a mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either one means they can be
>>>>>>>> marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

>>>>>>>>> Thanks as always for the update.
>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more
>>>>>>>>> than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change
>>>>>>>>> to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are
>>>>>>>>> used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the
>>>>>>>>> settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it,
>>>>>>>>> instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be
>>>>>>>>> used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails
>>>>>>>>> for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect
>>>>>>>>> we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making
>>>>>>>>> updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the
>>>>>>>>> following system:
>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
>>>>>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the
>>>>>>>>>    title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks,
>>>>>>>>>    fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on
>>>>>>>>>    activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that
>>>>>>>>>    don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate
>>>>>>>>>    a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An
>>>>>>>>>    alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated
>>>>>>>>>    scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d
>>>>>>>>>    like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the
>>>>>>>>>    context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields
>>>>>>>>>    within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> On the other issues:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - The news filters have been notoriously finicky from
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    page to page. I've sorted it out now--the "showNews" logic just needed to
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    be tweaked a bit.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - In terms of the slow load times, I've been seeing the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    same thing and this is last on my list to test and optimize after
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    everything else is in place. Part of this will be fixing the placeholders
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    which aren't resolving currently and you're right that production should
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    improve it some.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - Forestry page, the spacing and fonts have changed how
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    they work from 1.9:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *v1.9 uses fixed design tokens defined
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       in tailwind.config.js (discrete spacing scale; static text sizes). v4
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       switches to CSS variables and formulas — spacing becomes “any integer
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       × --spacing,” and text sizes/line-heights come from --text-*variables —
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       while prose works the same but plugs into the new variable system.*
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - For instance, the old system
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = 2rem (32px), p-4 = 1rem (16px) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - The new system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = calc(var(--spacing) * 8)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>                 p-4 = calc(var(--spacing) * 4) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - I've been working on the base styling and I
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       think I have things restored--there may still be some outliers. I removed
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       the spacing definitions in app.pcss @theme section, which was a carryover
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       from the tailwind.config.js v1.9 but seems to be interfering with the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       styling we want now.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - The accessibility checker issues:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Four landmark issues*:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation--top.vue has the <div
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          class="flex-grow">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation-item--secondary.twig has the <span>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          Activity Calendar </span>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - To fix this accessibility issue I added a <nav>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          as a parent element to main navigation, main navigation items and "utility
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          navigation items" for the secondary nav items which are all labelled now
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          with aria-label
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Modal Accessible Name*:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - modal--main.vue had this code and I added an
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          aria-label fallback with a dynamic switch for each modal type and passed
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          the ID down to the component children which should ensure consistency for
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          Screen Readers.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Role Usage on Nav--Items*: the code referenced is
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       in navigation--items.vue and the problem has to do with the menu role
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       usage. The menu role shouldn't be necessary here since we're using a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       semantic nav element with a descriptive aria-label so I just removed the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       roles and this should be clean now.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> All that's left on my list now is the performance issues
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> with slow load times and placeholder usage.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > For point #3 in my last email regarding using alt=“null” vs populating the alt text with a file name, I re-read the WCAG spec and I think we’d be better off making the fallback alt=“”. While this may trip up automted scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument that most images on the site do NOT convey essential information and serve a mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either one means they can be marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Thanks as always for the update.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following system:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Okay, that clarification made quick work of three items--so I really appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up on since the fixes are all Craft > Settings solutions. Here are the 3 items and solutions:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Originally Item #2: Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example: https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times (see attached).
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. Originally Item #3: Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. Originally Item #5: The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > These will all need to be addressed as last minute items since the "allowAdminChanges" must be on, which means we'll need to use a production database in staging, then pushed to production with the other updates.

>>>>>>> definitely good news! Hopefully the auto-popup works. When I last discussed
>>>>>>> this with Aspen, the understanding was that the staff would need to be
>>>>>>> trained on how to enter the alt text as part of their process, and the
>>>>>>> impetus would be on them to make sure it gets done. If there’s a way when
>>>>>>> uploading images as part of other entries to force the alt text, that’s
>>>>>>> even better.
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> Regarding the alt text settings per directory, I think we just need
>>>>>>> to enable alt text across the board in all media directories. It should be
>>>>>>> *required* for the following:
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> Galleries
>>>>>>> Teasers
>>>>>>> Sliders
>>>>>>> Hero Images
>>>>>>> Articles (possibly?)
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> I’m still thoroughly confused as to why Mark set up many
>>>>>>> directories. Some aren’t actively in use from what I see (Documents, Cover
>>>>>>> photos, Open Graph Images). Others seem to be used inconsistently (i.e. the
>>>>>>> PDFs folder often ends up with images in there). The directories don’t seem
>>>>>>> well organized, and stuff has a habit of going into the wrong directory
>>>>>>> anyway, hence why I think alt text should at least be an option for ALL
>>>>>>> media, but only required in the folders in which image content is the
>>>>>>> primary content allowed. If that proves to be an issue, please let me know.
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> Is there a centralized location in Craft where we can view what
>>>>>>> entries store conent in which media folders, or is that addressed on a
>>>>>>> field by field basis? If there’s a central location, I’d like to take a
>>>>>>> look at that.
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> For point #3 in my last email regarding using alt=“null” vs
>>>>>>> populating the alt text with a file name, I re-read the WCAG spec and I
>>>>>>> think we’d be better off making the fallback alt=“”. While this may trip up
>>>>>>> automted scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument
>>>>>>> that most images on the site do NOT convey essential information and serve
>>>>>>> a mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either one means they can be
>>>>>>> marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> If you run into any questions or have any concerns about that
>>>>>>> approach, please let me know.

>>>>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than
>>>>>>>> a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to
>>>>>>>> the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are
>>>>>>>> used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the
>>>>>>>> settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it,
>>>>>>>> instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be
>>>>>>>> used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails
>>>>>>>> for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect
>>>>>>>> we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making
>>>>>>>> updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the
>>>>>>>> following system:
>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
>>>>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the
>>>>>>>>    title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks,
>>>>>>>>    fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on
>>>>>>>>    activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that
>>>>>>>>    don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate
>>>>>>>>    a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An
>>>>>>>>    alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated
>>>>>>>>    scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d
>>>>>>>>    like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the
>>>>>>>>    context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields
>>>>>>>>    within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    which aren't resolving currently and you're right that production should
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    improve it some.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - Forestry page, the spacing and fonts have changed how
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    they work from 1.9:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *v1.9 uses fixed design tokens defined
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       in tailwind.config.js (discrete spacing scale; static text sizes). v4
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       switches to CSS variables and formulas — spacing becomes “any integer
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       × --spacing,” and text sizes/line-heights come from --text-*variables —
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       while prose works the same but plugs into the new variable system.*
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - For instance, the old system
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = 2rem (32px), p-4 = 1rem (16px) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - The new system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = calc(var(--spacing) * 8)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>                 p-4 = calc(var(--spacing) * 4) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - I've been working on the base styling and I think
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       I have things restored--there may still be some outliers. I removed the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       spacing definitions in app.pcss @theme section, which was a carryover from
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       the tailwind.config.js v1.9 but seems to be interfering with the styling we
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       want now.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - The accessibility checker issues:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Four landmark issues*:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation--top.vue has the <div
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          class="flex-grow">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation-item--secondary.twig has the <span>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          Activity Calendar </span>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - To fix this accessibility issue I added a <nav>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          as a parent element to main navigation, main navigation items and "utility
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          navigation items" for the secondary nav items which are all labelled now
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          with aria-label
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Modal Accessible Name*:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - modal--main.vue had this code and I added an
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          aria-label fallback with a dynamic switch for each modal type and passed
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          the ID down to the component children which should ensure consistency for
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>          Screen Readers.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Role Usage on Nav--Items*: the code referenced is
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       in navigation--items.vue and the problem has to do with the menu role
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       usage. The menu role shouldn't be necessary here since we're using a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       semantic nav element with a descriptive aria-label so I just removed the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>       roles and this should be clean now.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > For point #3 in my last email regarding using alt=“null” vs populating the alt text with a file name, I re-read the WCAG spec and I think we’d be better off making the fallback alt=“”. While this may trip up automted scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument that most images on the site do NOT convey essential information and serve a mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either one means they can be marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following system:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Originally Item #2: Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example: https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times (see attached).
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. Originally Item #3: Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. Originally Item #5: The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)

The reason for the mismatch is a simple naming convention. The neutral outline color in the old code was outline-gray and in the new code we redefine the color variable rather than swap them out to fit each outline case. This was in part to avoid the repeated use of !important to override variables for particular instances which would occasionally result in unforeseen behavior--making the code a bit cleaner. To fix it, I'll just change the naming convention to "outline-base" to avoid confusion. This is a quick and easy change too if you have a different naming convention you prefer.

>>>>>> Hi Eric,
>>>>>>
>>>>>> If there’s a way encourage filling of the alt text, that’s definitely
>>>>>> good news! Hopefully the auto-popup works. When I last discussed this with
>>>>>> Aspen, the understanding was that the staff would need to be trained on how
>>>>>> to enter the alt text as part of their process, and the impetus would be on
>>>>>> them to make sure it gets done. If there’s a way when uploading images as
>>>>>> part of other entries to force the alt text, that’s even better.
>>>>>>
>>>>>> Regarding the alt text settings per directory, I think we just need
>>>>>> to enable alt text across the board in all media directories. It should be
>>>>>> *required* for the following:
>>>>>>
>>>>>> Galleries
>>>>>> Teasers
>>>>>> Sliders
>>>>>> Hero Images
>>>>>> Articles (possibly?)
>>>>>>
>>>>>> I’m still thoroughly confused as to why Mark set up many directories.
>>>>>> Some aren’t actively in use from what I see (Documents, Cover photos, Open
>>>>>> Graph Images). Others seem to be used inconsistently (i.e. the PDFs folder
>>>>>> often ends up with images in there). The directories don’t seem well
>>>>>> organized, and stuff has a habit of going into the wrong directory anyway,
>>>>>> hence why I think alt text should at least be an option for ALL media, but
>>>>>> only required in the folders in which image content is the primary content
>>>>>> allowed. If that proves to be an issue, please let me know.
>>>>>>
>>>>>> Is there a centralized location in Craft where we can view what
>>>>>> entries store conent in which media folders, or is that addressed on a
>>>>>> field by field basis? If there’s a central location, I’d like to take a
>>>>>> look at that.
>>>>>>
>>>>>> For point #3 in my last email regarding using alt=“null” vs
>>>>>> populating the alt text with a file name, I re-read the WCAG spec and I
>>>>>> think we’d be better off making the fallback alt=“”. While this may trip up
>>>>>> automted scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument
>>>>>> that most images on the site do NOT convey essential information and serve
>>>>>> a mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either one means they can be
>>>>>> marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
>>>>>>
>>>>>> If you run into any questions or have any concerns about that
>>>>>> approach, please let me know.
>>>>>>

>>>>>> On Wed, Sep 24, 2025 at 9:58 PM Shaun Cooney | Monument Graphics <
>>>>>> shaun@monumentgraphics.com> wrote:
>>>>>>
>>>>>>> Thanks as always for the update.
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than
>>>>>>> a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to
>>>>>>> the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are
>>>>>>> used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the
>>>>>>> settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it,
>>>>>>> instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be
>>>>>>> used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails
>>>>>>> for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect
>>>>>>> we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making
>>>>>>> updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following
>>>>>>> system:
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
>>>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title
>>>>>>>    of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks,
>>>>>>>    fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on
>>>>>>>    activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that
>>>>>>>    don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate
>>>>>>>    a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An
>>>>>>>    alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated
>>>>>>>    scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d
>>>>>>>    like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the
>>>>>>>    context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields
>>>>>>>    within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> Let me know what you think….
>>>>>>>
>>>>>>> In the meantime, I’ll start reviewing dev for the other items.

>>>>>>>>> solutions:
>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>    1. *Originally Item #2*: Remove the “Daily" repeating option
>>>>>>>>>    for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the
>>>>>>>>>    simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times,
>>>>>>>>>    someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray.
>>>>>>>>>    This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the
>>>>>>>>>    “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example:
>>>>>>>>>    https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times
>>>>>>>>>    (see attached).
>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields > Dropdown >
>>>>>>>>>       Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest option without
>>>>>>>>>       causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value
>>>>>>>>>    2. *Originally Item #3*: Require cancellations within
>>>>>>>>>    classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank
>>>>>>>>>    cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting
>>>>>>>>>    one of the fields therein to be required?
>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields > Events >
>>>>>>>>>       Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
>>>>>>>>>    3. *Originally Item #5*: The list of selectable locations for
>>>>>>>>>    classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add
>>>>>>>>>    those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in
>>>>>>>>>    the calendar grid and within the modals?
>>>>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields > Entries >
>>>>>>>>>       Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will allow
>>>>>>>>>       abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)
>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>> These will all need to be addressed as last minute items since the
>>>>>>>>> "allowAdminChanges" must be on, which means we'll need to use a production
>>>>>>>>> database in staging, then pushed to production with the other updates.

>>>>>>>>> the solutions while you're looking over the site.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - The news filters have been notoriously finicky from page

>>>>>>>>>>>>>    tweaked a bit.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - In terms of the slow load times, I've been seeing the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>    same thing and this is last on my list to test and optimize after
>>>>>>>>>>>>>    everything else is in place. Part of this will be fixing the placeholders
>>>>>>>>>>>>>    which aren't resolving currently and you're right that production should
>>>>>>>>>>>>>    improve it some.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - Forestry page, the spacing and fonts have changed how
>>>>>>>>>>>>>    they work from 1.9:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *v1.9 uses fixed design tokens defined
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       in tailwind.config.js (discrete spacing scale; static text sizes). v4
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       switches to CSS variables and formulas — spacing becomes “any integer
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       × --spacing,” and text sizes/line-heights come from --text-*variables —
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       while prose works the same but plugs into the new variable system.*
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - For instance, the old system
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = 2rem (32px), p-4 = 1rem (16px) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - The new system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = calc(var(--spacing) * 8)
>>>>>>>>>>>>>                 p-4 = calc(var(--spacing) * 4) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - I've been working on the base styling and I think
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       I have things restored--there may still be some outliers. I removed the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       spacing definitions in app.pcss @theme section, which was a carryover from
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       the tailwind.config.js v1.9 but seems to be interfering with the styling we
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       want now.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>    - The accessibility checker issues:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Four landmark issues*:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation--top.vue has the <div
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          class="flex-grow">
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation-item--secondary.twig has the <span>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          Activity Calendar </span>
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - To fix this accessibility issue I added a <nav> as
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          a parent element to main navigation, main navigation items and "utility
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          navigation items" for the secondary nav items which are all labelled now
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          with aria-label
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Modal Accessible Name*:
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          - modal--main.vue had this code and I added an
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          aria-label fallback with a dynamic switch for each modal type and passed
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          the ID down to the component children which should ensure consistency for
>>>>>>>>>>>>>          Screen Readers.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Role Usage on Nav--Items*: the code referenced is in
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       navigation--items.vue and the problem has to do with the menu role usage.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       The menu role shouldn't be necessary here since we're using a semantic nav
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       element with a descriptive aria-label so I just removed the roles and this
>>>>>>>>>>>>>       should be clean now.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>> All that's left on my list now is the performance issues with
>>>>>>>>>>>>> slow load times and placeholder usage.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following system:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Okay, that clarification made quick work of three items--so I really appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up on since the fixes are all Craft > Settings solutions. Here are the 3 items and solutions:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Originally Item #2: Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example: https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times (see attached).
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. Originally Item #3: Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. Originally Item #5: The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 4. I believe this one was on a checklist from a few months ago so thanks for bringing it up again. The reason for the mismatch is a simple naming convention. The neutral outline color in the old code was outline-gray and in the new code we redefine the color variable rather than swap them out to fit each outline case. This was in part to avoid the repeated use of !important to override variables for particular instances which would occasionally result in unforeseen behavior--making the code a bit cleaner. To fix it, I'll just change the naming convention to "outline-base" to avoid confusion. This is a quick and easy change too if you have a different naming convention you prefer.

>>>>> scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument that
>>>>> most images on the site do NOT convey essential information and serve a
>>>>> mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either one means they can be
>>>>> marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
>>>>>
>>>>> If you run into any questions or have any concerns about that
>>>>> approach, please let me know.

>>>>>> Thanks as always for the update.
>>>>>>
>>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a
>>>>>> matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the
>>>>>> code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used,
>>>>>> both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the
>>>>>> settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it,
>>>>>> instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be
>>>>>> used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails
>>>>>> for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect
>>>>>> we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making
>>>>>> updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>>
>>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following
>>>>>> system:
>>>>>>
>>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
>>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title
>>>>>>    of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks,
>>>>>>    fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on
>>>>>>    activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that
>>>>>>    don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate
>>>>>>    a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An
>>>>>>    alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated
>>>>>>    scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d
>>>>>>    like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the
>>>>>>    context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields
>>>>>>    within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

>>>>>>>>       causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value

>>>>>>>>>>>> On the other issues:
>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>>    - The news filters have been notoriously finicky from page
>>>>>>>>>>>>    to page. I've sorted it out now--the "showNews" logic just needed to be
>>>>>>>>>>>>    tweaked a bit.
>>>>>>>>>>>>    - In terms of the slow load times, I've been seeing the
>>>>>>>>>>>>    same thing and this is last on my list to test and optimize after
>>>>>>>>>>>>    everything else is in place. Part of this will be fixing the placeholders
>>>>>>>>>>>>    which aren't resolving currently and you're right that production should
>>>>>>>>>>>>    improve it some.
>>>>>>>>>>>>    - Forestry page, the spacing and fonts have changed how
>>>>>>>>>>>>    they work from 1.9:
>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *v1.9 uses fixed design tokens defined
>>>>>>>>>>>>       in tailwind.config.js (discrete spacing scale; static text sizes). v4
>>>>>>>>>>>>       switches to CSS variables and formulas — spacing becomes “any integer
>>>>>>>>>>>>       × --spacing,” and text sizes/line-heights come from --text-*variables —
>>>>>>>>>>>>       while prose works the same but plugs into the new variable system.*
>>>>>>>>>>>>       - For instance, the old system
>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = 2rem (32px), p-4 = 1rem (16px) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>          - The new system:
>>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = calc(var(--spacing) * 8)
>>>>>>>>>>>>                 p-4 = calc(var(--spacing) * 4) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>>          - I've been working on the base styling and I think I
>>>>>>>>>>>>       have things restored--there may still be some outliers. I removed the
>>>>>>>>>>>>       spacing definitions in app.pcss @theme section, which was a carryover from
>>>>>>>>>>>>       the tailwind.config.js v1.9 but seems to be interfering with the styling we
>>>>>>>>>>>>       want now.
>>>>>>>>>>>>    - The accessibility checker issues:
>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Four landmark issues*:
>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation--top.vue has the <div class="flex-grow">
>>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation-item--secondary.twig has the <span>
>>>>>>>>>>>>          Activity Calendar </span>
>>>>>>>>>>>>          - To fix this accessibility issue I added a <nav> as
>>>>>>>>>>>>          a parent element to main navigation, main navigation items and "utility
>>>>>>>>>>>>          navigation items" for the secondary nav items which are all labelled now
>>>>>>>>>>>>          with aria-label
>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Modal Accessible Name*:
>>>>>>>>>>>>          - modal--main.vue had this code and I added an
>>>>>>>>>>>>          aria-label fallback with a dynamic switch for each modal type and passed
>>>>>>>>>>>>          the ID down to the component children which should ensure consistency for
>>>>>>>>>>>>          Screen Readers.
>>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Role Usage on Nav--Items*: the code referenced is in
>>>>>>>>>>>>       navigation--items.vue and the problem has to do with the menu role usage.
>>>>>>>>>>>>       The menu role shouldn't be necessary here since we're using a semantic nav
>>>>>>>>>>>>       element with a descriptive aria-label so I just removed the roles and this
>>>>>>>>>>>>       should be clean now.
>>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>> All that's left on my list now is the performance issues with
>>>>>>>>>>>> slow load times and placeholder usage.

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    4. I believe this one was on a checklist from a few
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    months ago so thanks for bringing it up again. The reason for the mismatch
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    is a simple naming convention. The neutral outline color in the old code
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    was outline-gray and in the new code we redefine the color variable rather
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    than swap them out to fit each outline case. This was in part to avoid the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    repeated use of !important to override variables for particular instances
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    which would occasionally result in unforeseen behavior--making the code a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    bit cleaner. To fix it, I'll just change the naming convention to
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    "outline-base" to avoid confusion. This is a quick and easy change too if
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    you have a different naming convention you prefer.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    5. Thanks for noting this. Before the update we used
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    focus:outline-* as inline css; however, with the new Tailwind set up we use
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the outline-* directly and the focus is implied.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    6. Gotcha. Yeah, this was in the aspect-ratio
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    troubleshooting. I reintroduced xl:h-full to the <picture> element and that
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    fixed it.

> > > > > > > > > > > For point #3 in my last email regarding using alt=“null” vs populating the alt text with a file name, I re-read the WCAG spec and I think we’d be better off making the fallback alt=“”. While this may trip up automted scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument that most images on the site do NOT convey essential information and serve a mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either one means they can be marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following system:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Okay, that clarification made quick work of three items--so I really appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up on since the fixes are all Craft > Settings solutions. Here are the 3 items and solutions:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Originally Item #2: Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example: https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times (see attached).
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. Originally Item #3: Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. Originally Item #5: The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >

The reason for the mismatch is a simple naming convention. The neutral outline color in the old code was outline-gray and in the new code we redefine the color variable rather than swap them out to fit each outline case. This was in part to avoid the repeated use of !important to override variables for particular instances which would occasionally result in unforeseen behavior--making the code a bit cleaner. To fix it, I'll just change the naming convention to "outline-base" to avoid confusion. This is a quick and easy change too if you have a different naming convention you prefer.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 5. Thanks for noting this. Before the update we used focus:outline-* as inline css; however, with the new Tailwind set up we use the outline-* directly and the focus is implied.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 6. Gotcha. Yeah, this was in the aspect-ratio troubleshooting. I reintroduced xl:h-full to the <picture> element and that fixed it.

>>>> Teasers

>>>> scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument that

>>>> marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

>>>>> Thanks as always for the update.
>>>>>
>>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a
>>>>> matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the
>>>>> code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used,
>>>>> both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the
>>>>> settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it,
>>>>> instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be
>>>>> used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails
>>>>> for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect
>>>>> we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making
>>>>> updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>>
>>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following
>>>>> system:
>>>>>
>>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
>>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title
>>>>>    of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks,
>>>>>    fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on
>>>>>    activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that
>>>>>    don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate
>>>>>    a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An
>>>>>    alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated
>>>>>    scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d
>>>>>    like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the
>>>>>    context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields
>>>>>    within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

>>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>>    - The news filters have been notoriously finicky from page
>>>>>>>>>>>    to page. I've sorted it out now--the "showNews" logic just needed to be
>>>>>>>>>>>    tweaked a bit.
>>>>>>>>>>>    - In terms of the slow load times, I've been seeing the same
>>>>>>>>>>>    thing and this is last on my list to test and optimize after everything
>>>>>>>>>>>    else is in place. Part of this will be fixing the placeholders which aren't
>>>>>>>>>>>    resolving currently and you're right that production should improve it
>>>>>>>>>>>    some.
>>>>>>>>>>>    - Forestry page, the spacing and fonts have changed how they
>>>>>>>>>>>    work from 1.9:
>>>>>>>>>>>       - *v1.9 uses fixed design tokens defined
>>>>>>>>>>>       in tailwind.config.js (discrete spacing scale; static text sizes). v4
>>>>>>>>>>>       switches to CSS variables and formulas — spacing becomes “any integer
>>>>>>>>>>>       × --spacing,” and text sizes/line-heights come from --text-*variables —
>>>>>>>>>>>       while prose works the same but plugs into the new variable system.*
>>>>>>>>>>>       - For instance, the old system
>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = 2rem (32px), p-4 = 1rem (16px) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>          - The new system:
>>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = calc(var(--spacing) * 8)
>>>>>>>>>>>                 p-4 = calc(var(--spacing) * 4) -->
>>>>>>>>>>>          - I've been working on the base styling and I think I
>>>>>>>>>>>       have things restored--there may still be some outliers. I removed the
>>>>>>>>>>>       spacing definitions in app.pcss @theme section, which was a carryover from
>>>>>>>>>>>       the tailwind.config.js v1.9 but seems to be interfering with the styling we
>>>>>>>>>>>       want now.
>>>>>>>>>>>    - The accessibility checker issues:
>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Four landmark issues*:
>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation--top.vue has the <div class="flex-grow">
>>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation-item--secondary.twig has the <span>
>>>>>>>>>>>          Activity Calendar </span>
>>>>>>>>>>>          - To fix this accessibility issue I added a <nav> as a
>>>>>>>>>>>          parent element to main navigation, main navigation items and "utility
>>>>>>>>>>>          navigation items" for the secondary nav items which are all labelled now
>>>>>>>>>>>          with aria-label
>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Modal Accessible Name*:
>>>>>>>>>>>          - modal--main.vue had this code and I added an
>>>>>>>>>>>          aria-label fallback with a dynamic switch for each modal type and passed
>>>>>>>>>>>          the ID down to the component children which should ensure consistency for
>>>>>>>>>>>          Screen Readers.
>>>>>>>>>>>       - *Role Usage on Nav--Items*: the code referenced is in
>>>>>>>>>>>       navigation--items.vue and the problem has to do with the menu role usage.
>>>>>>>>>>>       The menu role shouldn't be necessary here since we're using a semantic nav

>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    months ago so thanks for bringing it up again. The reason for the mismatch
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    is a simple naming convention. The neutral outline color in the old code
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    was outline-gray and in the new code we redefine the color variable rather
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    than swap them out to fit each outline case. This was in part to avoid the
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    repeated use of !important to override variables for particular instances
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    which would occasionally result in unforeseen behavior--making the code a
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    bit cleaner. To fix it, I'll just change the naming convention to
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    "outline-base" to avoid confusion. This is a quick and easy change too if
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    you have a different naming convention you prefer.
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    5. Thanks for noting this. Before the update we used
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    focus:outline-* as inline css; however, with the new Tailwind set up we use
>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>    the outline-* directly and the focus is implied.

Either one means they can be marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.

> > > > > > > > > > > Thanks as always for the update.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following system:
> > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > 1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
> > > > > > > > > > > 2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
> > > > > > > > > > > 3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > Okay, that clarification made quick work of three items--so I really appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up on since the fixes are all Craft > Settings solutions. Here are the 3 items and solutions:
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Originally Item #2: Remove the “Daily" repeating option for all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray. This is found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the “Days/Times” tab. Here’s an example: https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times (see attached).
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Dropdown > Repeat Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest option without causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. Originally Item #3: Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. Originally Item #5: The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Entries > Location Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will allow abbreviations to be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 4. I believe this one was on a checklist from a few months ago so thanks for bringing it up again. The reason for the mismatch is a simple naming convention. The neutral outline color in the old code was outline-gray and in the new code we redefine the color variable rather than swap them out to fit each outline case. This was in part to avoid the repeated use of !important to override variables for particular instances which would occasionally result in unforeseen behavior--making the code a bit cleaner. To fix it, I'll just change the naming convention to "outline-base" to avoid confusion. This is a quick and easy change too if you have a different naming convention you prefer.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 5. Thanks for noting this. Before the update we used focus:outline-* as inline css; however, with the new Tailwind set up we use the outline-* directly and the focus is implied.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 6. Gotcha. Yeah, this was in the aspect-ratio troubleshooting. I reintroduced xl:h-full to the <picture> element and that fixed it.

>>> *required* for the following:
>>>
>>> Galleries
>>> Teasers
>>> Sliders
>>> Hero Images
>>> Articles (possibly?)
>>>
>>> I’m still thoroughly confused as to why Mark set up many directories.
>>> Some aren’t actively in use from what I see (Documents, Cover photos, Open
>>> Graph Images). Others seem to be used inconsistently (i.e. the PDFs folder
>>> often ends up with images in there). The directories don’t seem well
>>> organized, and stuff has a habit of going into the wrong directory anyway,
>>> hence why I think alt text should at least be an option for ALL media, but

>>> allowed. If that proves to be an issue, please let me know.

>>> better off making the fallback alt=“”. While this may trip up automted
>>> scanners, more often than not, I think one could make the argument that
>>> most images on the site do NOT convey essential information and serve a
>>> mostly decorative, or repetative purpose. Either one means they can be
>>> marked with a null value (alt=“”) and meet WCAG 2.2 AA.
>>>
>>> If you run into any questions or have any concerns about that approach,
>>> please let me know.

>>>> Thanks as always for the update.
>>>>
>>>> The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a
>>>> matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the
>>>> code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used,
>>>> both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the
>>>> settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it,
>>>> instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be
>>>> used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails
>>>> for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect
>>>> we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making
>>>> updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>>
>>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following
>>>> system:
>>>>
>>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
>>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of
>>>>    the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields,
>>>>    trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on
>>>>    activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that
>>>>    don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate
>>>>    a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An
>>>>    alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated
>>>>    scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d
>>>>    like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the
>>>>    context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields
>>>>    within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.
>>>>
>>>> Let me know what you think….
>>>>
>>>> In the meantime, I’ll start reviewing dev for the other items.
>>>>

>>>>>> appreciate that--which I wanted to give you a heads up on since the fixes
>>>>>> are all Craft > Settings solutions. Here are the 3 items and solutions:
>>>>>>
>>>>>>    1. *Originally Item #2*: Remove the “Daily" repeating option for
>>>>>>    all events. If you think that might cause issues with the code, the simpler
>>>>>>    solution would be to set “Weekly” as the default. Too many times, someone
>>>>>>    forgets to change this, and it throws the calendar into disarray. This is
>>>>>>    found in the Classes/Events and Leagues entries under the “Days/Times” tab.
>>>>>>    Here’s an example:
>>>>>>    https://www.aspenrecreation.com/admin/entries/activityEvents/24076-learn-to-swim-level-1-saturday-august#tab02--days-times
>>>>>>    (see attached).
>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields > Dropdown > Repeat
>>>>>>       Frequency > check default Weekly (safest and quickest option without
>>>>>>       causing unintended breakage for entries that already use the “daily” value
>>>>>>    2. *Originally Item #3*: Require cancellations within
>>>>>>    classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank
>>>>>>    cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting
>>>>>>    one of the fields therein to be required?
>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields > Events >
>>>>>>       Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
>>>>>>    3. *Originally Item #5*: The list of selectable locations for
>>>>>>    classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add
>>>>>>    those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in
>>>>>>    the calendar grid and within the modals?
>>>>>>       - *Solution*: Update in Settings > Fields > Entries > Location
>>>>>>       Select > Sources: check “Athletic Fields” (this will allow abbreviations to
>>>>>>       be used in the same way and page locations site-wide)
>>>>>>
>>>>>> These will all need to be addressed as last minute items since the
>>>>>> "allowAdminChanges" must be on, which means we'll need to use a production
>>>>>> database in staging, then pushed to production with the other updates.
>>>>>>

>>>>>> solutions while you're looking over the site.

>>>>>>>>>> On the other issues:
>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>>    - The news filters have been notoriously finicky from page to
>>>>>>>>>>    page. I've sorted it out now--the "showNews" logic just needed to be
>>>>>>>>>>    tweaked a bit.
>>>>>>>>>>    - In terms of the slow load times, I've been seeing the same
>>>>>>>>>>    thing and this is last on my list to test and optimize after everything
>>>>>>>>>>    else is in place. Part of this will be fixing the placeholders which aren't
>>>>>>>>>>    resolving currently and you're right that production should improve it
>>>>>>>>>>    some.
>>>>>>>>>>    - Forestry page, the spacing and fonts have changed how they
>>>>>>>>>>    work from 1.9:
>>>>>>>>>>       - *v1.9 uses fixed design tokens defined
>>>>>>>>>>       in tailwind.config.js (discrete spacing scale; static text sizes). v4
>>>>>>>>>>       switches to CSS variables and formulas — spacing becomes “any integer
>>>>>>>>>>       × --spacing,” and text sizes/line-heights come from --text-*variables —
>>>>>>>>>>       while prose works the same but plugs into the new variable system.*
>>>>>>>>>>       - For instance, the old system
>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = 2rem (32px), p-4 = 1rem (16px) -->
>>>>>>>>>>          - The new system:
>>>>>>>>>>          - <div class="mt-8 p-4">
>>>>>>>>>>            <!-- mt-8 = calc(var(--spacing) * 8)
>>>>>>>>>>                 p-4 = calc(var(--spacing) * 4) -->
>>>>>>>>>>          - I've been working on the base styling and I think I
>>>>>>>>>>       have things restored--there may still be some outliers. I removed the
>>>>>>>>>>       spacing definitions in app.pcss @theme section, which was a carryover from
>>>>>>>>>>       the tailwind.config.js v1.9 but seems to be interfering with the styling we
>>>>>>>>>>       want now.
>>>>>>>>>>    - The accessibility checker issues:
>>>>>>>>>>       - *Four landmark issues*:
>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation--top.vue has the <div class="flex-grow">
>>>>>>>>>>          - navigation-item--secondary.twig has the <span>
>>>>>>>>>>          Activity Calendar </span>
>>>>>>>>>>          - To fix this accessibility issue I added a <nav> as a
>>>>>>>>>>          parent element to main navigation, main navigation items and "utility
>>>>>>>>>>          navigation items" for the secondary nav items which are all labelled now
>>>>>>>>>>          with aria-label
>>>>>>>>>>       - *Modal Accessible Name*:
>>>>>>>>>>          - modal--main.vue had this code and I added an
>>>>>>>>>>          aria-label fallback with a dynamic switch for each modal type and passed
>>>>>>>>>>          the ID down to the component children which should ensure consistency for
>>>>>>>>>>          Screen Readers.
>>>>>>>>>>       - *Role Usage on Nav--Items*: the code referenced is in
>>>>>>>>>>       navigation--items.vue and the problem has to do with the menu role usage.
>>>>>>>>>>       The menu role shouldn't be necessary here since we're using a semantic nav
>>>>>>>>>>       element with a descriptive aria-label so I just removed the roles and this
>>>>>>>>>>       should be clean now.
>>>>>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>>> All that's left on my list now is the performance issues with
>>>>>>>>>> slow load times and placeholder usage.

Hi Eric,

Sounds like our lists are in agreement, so please keep plugging away.

The critical issues to address before deployment are the alt text and screen reader issues, as you indicated. > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > The item I’m most leary about is the alt text. That’ll be more than a matter of just enabling a field in settings or making a quick change to the code. It’ll most likely require tracking down everywhere images are used, both in the Craft settings and also in the code, and making sure the settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it, instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making updates in several places to cover all uses.
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following system:
> > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > 1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
> > > > > > > > 2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields, trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
> > > > > > > > 3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d like to make the alt text required, but we pobably can’t do that from the context that most images are uploaded, since they’re often added as fields within other entries, not directly to the media gallery.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 2. Originally Item #3: Require cancellations within classes/events to not be blank. When the calendar crashes, a blank cancellation is usually the culprit. Perhaps this could be fixed by setting one of the fields therein to be required?
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > >     • Solution: Update in Settings > Fields > Events > Cancellations > check “This field is required.”
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 3. Originally Item #5: The list of selectable locations for classes/events doesn’t include the athletic fields. Is it possible to add those and display these locations on the calendar as the abbreviations in the calendar grid and within the modals?

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > >
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 1. Got it. That color is corrected.

> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 4. I believe this one was on a checklist from a few months ago so thanks for bringing it up again. The reason for the mismatch is a simple naming convention. The neutral outline color in the old code was outline-gray and in the new code we redefine the color variable rather than swap them out to fit each outline case. This was in part to avoid the repeated use of !important to override variables for particular instances which would occasionally result in unforeseen behavior--making the code a bit cleaner. To fix it, I'll just change the naming convention to "outline-base" to avoid confusion. This is a quick and easy change too if you have a different naming convention you prefer.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 5. Thanks for noting this. Before the update we used focus:outline-* as inline css; however, with the new Tailwind set up we use the outline-* directly and the focus is implied.
> > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > > 6. Gotcha. Yeah, this was in the aspect-ratio troubleshooting. I reintroduced xl:h-full to the <picture> element and that fixed it.

>>> settings for alt text are enabled AND the code is configured to render it,
>>> instead of defaulting to the file name or entry title. Since images can be
>>> used in so many contexts—from hero and featured page images to thumbnails
>>> for parks, trails, fields, news items, blog entries, and more, I expect
>>> we’ll need to spend some time tracking all possible uses down and making
>>> updates in several places to cover all uses.
>>>
>>> In most cases, I believe the best approach will be use the following
>>> system:
>>>
>>>    1. If alt text is supplied for the image, render the alt text.
>>>    2. If no alt text is supplied, fill the alt field with the title of
>>>    the entry for any type of facility or person (rec centers, parks, fields,
>>>    trails, staff, instructors, etc.)
>>>    3. For other images, such as hero images, featured images on
>>>    activity pages, and images that are part of a user-created gallery that
>>>    don’t have alt text, I lean toward using a null value (alt=“”) to indicate
>>>    a decorative image, as more often than not, that’s what they are. An
>>>    alternative could be to use the file name, which would make automated
>>>    scanners happier. I’m open to your thoughts on this though. Ideally, I’d
